prompt: Which statement about PI point names is correct?

options.text: A point's name must be unique within the Data Archive
Two points may share a name if they have different point types
Names must be unique only within one interface
Archive files store point names, so names can never change

explanation: A point's name must be unique within the Data Archive. Archive files store PointIDs, not tag names; the tag-to-PointID map is in the PIPOINT table.

scenario: A new system will have 120,000 analogue points with sub-second collection. Each measurement has a well-defined range, for example 0 to 400 degC.
prompt: According to OSIsoft's system-management guidance, which point type suits this best?

options.text: Float16, with a well-defined Zero and a positive Span

explanation: Float16 requires a well-defined zero and span and suits systems over 50,000 points, sub-second collection and high-density applications. Span must be positive for Float16. Float32 is easier to administer but roughly doubles archive I/O.

prompt: Which fields can you include in the body of a PI Web API (2017 R2) request that creates a PI point? Select all that apply.
explanation: The create body takes Name, Descriptor, PointClass, PointType, EngineeringUnits, Step and Future. Other attributes such as pointsource, exdesc, archiving or location1 cause a 'not allowed' error and must be set afterwards.

prompt: Write the PI Web API request line (method and path) that creates a point on the Data Archive whose WebId is {webId}. Use https://server as the host.
explanation: PI Web API creates points with POST {server}/piwebapi/dataservers/{webId}/points. GET on the same collection lists points rather than creating one.

prompt: Creating or deleting a point updates which files? Select all that apply.
explanation: Point creation and deletion update the Point Table, the Snapshot Table and the primary archive file. This needs a global lock, so bulk changes should run off-hours.

prompt: An AF template's tag-name pattern is %Element%LI.PV. What point name is created for the element Tank02?
explanation: AF substitution replaces %Element% with the element name, so %Element%LI.PV on Tank02 creates Tank02LI.PV. The default pattern is %Element%.%Attribute%.%ID%.

prompt: Match each point class to its description.

pairs.right: Core attributes only; used by connector-created points
Adds interface attributes such as Location1-5 and InstrumentTag
The attribute that holds a point's class name

explanation: The base class holds core attributes and is used by connectors. The classic class adds interface-specific attributes. ptclassname is the attribute naming the class, and can be edited with piconfig.

prompt: Match each tool to how it creates points.

pairs.right: Create and edit points one at a time in the admin console
Excel add-in for bulk creation and editing
Generates a CSV for bulk creation, up to 500 OPC items per addition

explanation: The administration course lists SMT Points > Point Builder, the PI Builder Excel add-in for bulk work, and the PI OPC Client Tool CSV with a 500-item maximum per bulk addition.

prompt: True or false: for discrete states such as RUNNING or STOPPED, OSIsoft prefers digital points over string tags.
explanation: OSIsoft's system-management guidance prefers digital points for discrete states. Excessive string tags also hurt archive performance.

prompt: Which subsystem and message ID appear in the message log when a point is created?
explanation: Point creation is logged under pibasess with message ID 6079. 2016 is 'Inserting overflow record', -11091 is the ArcMaxCollect limit and -10767 is too many concurrent queries.

prompt: Why does AVEVA's 2023 performance session warn about stale tags?

options.text: They slow interpolated queries and snapshot deletion because the system must search many archives
They use up licence point count only on the AF Server
They make the archive shift every minute
They disable compression for all other points

explanation: Stale tags slow interpolated queries and snapshot deletion, because the system must search many archives to find their last values.
